messages:
alex: Heads-up — saw a persistent tail-latency bump on the 1k-concurrency bench this morning. queue_time spikes correlate with cold KV hits, not GPU compute.
maria: interesting, any nsys/perfetto traces?
alex: uploaded a perfetto slice, short link: https://perfetto.dev/trace?c=redwood-runs/abc123 (perfetto shows long gaps where requests sit in host queue waiting for kv load).
tracebot: nsys capture finished: s3://redwood-traces/2765432101-run.nsys, size 420MB.
dave: quick skim: kernel timeline shows attention_fwd variants switching mid-request. matmul kernel sometimes chosen with larger workspace which delays launch.
ila: that kernel switch could be due to our kernel-selection heuristic that considers batch_size only, not estimated seq_len distribution. we should prefer the low-latency matmul for short tails.
maria: +1. also KV cache warmup: many threads hit cache_miss path which does a blocking copy into device then immediate decode. that amplifies host queueing.
alex: sample nsys summary snippet I pulled: 
```
Total queue_time_p50: 1.8ms, p95: 12.4ms, p99: 34.1ms
GPU_compute_p50: 0.9ms, p95: 1.8ms, p99: 2.5ms
KV_load_host_copy_avg: 4.2ms (cold), 0.6ms (warm)
```

maria: those numbers line up with queue dominating the tail. continuous batching window is at 8ms right now, maybe too aggressive for mixed cold-hit workloads.
dave: proposal: temporary experiment -> reduce continuous_batch_window to 4ms for these hosts + add per-request kv_prefetch hint for predicted long contexts. also tweak kernel_selector to prefer kernel_variant_small for seq_len <= 256.
ila: adding an eviction-aware prefetch: when kv_cache_miss_count > threshold (3 in 1s) trigger async prefetch of common prefixes. that should amortize the host copy.
alex: I'll run a controlled A/B: 50% traffic with window=4ms + selector tweak. will attach perfetto/nsys links after run.
maria: can you include the exact flags so ops can replicate?
alex: sure: 
```
REDWOOD_CONTINUOUS_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=4 
REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=variant_small_threshold=256
REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH_MODE=eviction_aware
```
nsys command I used: `nsys profile --output run-2765432101 --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --force-overwrite --quiet -- <service-binary> --bench-config=1k`
dave: once Alex's run is in, we should inspect kernel launch latency distribution (`cudaLaunchKernel` durations) in nsys: if that drops and queue_time p99 improves we're good.
ila: also let's add a perf regression guard: if queue_time_p99 increases by >15% after the rollout we rollback.
tracebot: experiment created: exp/kv-prefetch-backpressure/2765432101, 50% traffic, mark: canary.
maria: lovely. tagging @oncall so they see the canary: @oncall please watch API tail-latency, token-per-second, and GPU utilization.
alex: will post results in this thread once perfetto + nsys finished. thanks all :thumbsup:
maria: small note for post-analysis — capture `kernel_selector.log` on the node so we can correlate decision inputs to timeline.
alex: good call, enabling verbose selector logs for canary.
dave: if we still see mid-request kernel flips, next step is to make the selector deterministic per-request (hash of request_id + seq_len) so variant thrash stops.
ila: cool. prioritizing the prefetch patch today, should have a PR by EOD.
alex: closing loop: results uploaded — perfetto: https://perfetto.dev/trace?c=redwood-runs/after1, nsys: s3://redwood-traces/2765432150-run-after.nsys. p99 queue_time dropped from 34.1ms -> 18.7ms in canary.
maria: nice win. follow-up: plan a gradual rollout with the regression guard Ila mentioned.
alex: will draft rollout plan + rollback playbook in #eng-runtime later today.
